mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, let’s take a moment to bring it all together. Coping with loss and grief really is a personal journey—one that unfolds in its own time, and is shaped by love, memory, and the unique story of your life. There’s no single path, and no right or wrong way to mourn. What matters most is giving yourself permission to feel, to remember, and to heal at your own pace. So, here’s what I hope you’ll remember: Grief can be unpredictable and really personal—there’s no rulebook or universal timeline. Feelings like regret and guilt? They’re natural, and they do soften as you practice self-forgiveness and give yourself time. Community, culture, and rituals might bring comfort, but your own needs come first. If there are children or teens in your life, honesty, patience, and giving them space to share their feelings truly matters. And keeping a connection with those we’ve lost isn’t just okay—it can be deeply healing. If you’re in the midst of loss right now, please remember: you’re not alone. The pain may feel overwhelming, but that pain is proof of the love and connection you shared. Give yourself permission to grieve in your own way, and don’t hesitate to reach out—whether that’s to friends, family, professionals, or your community. Healing isn’t about letting go or forgetting; it’s about learning to carry your loss with grace, letting it become part of your story—without letting it overshadow everything else. In time, the sharpness of grief will soften, and you’ll find space for hope, meaning, and even joy. Trust that you have the strength to move forward, one gentle step at a time.
